stories.title: On Set with the Secret Spy
stories.subtitle: Behind the Scenes at Pinewood Studios
stories.narrative: At the famous movie studios, a bustling film crew prepares to shoot the climax of a new blockbuster thriller. In the story, a British secret spy undertakes an urgent mission to stop an evil billionaire from stealing digital codes. Behind the main cameras, a talented director uses technical expertise to direct every dramatic move. On set, a young actor checks high-tech gadgets before the clapperboard snaps. The director pauses to approve the lighting, and assistants quickly switch on powerful studio lamps while crew members switch off background alarms. In this top-secret facility, visitors are told that taking mobile photos is strictly forbidden. The prop team conducted an experiment with miniature laser pens, testing sophisticated props so that the dangerous scene looks completely real on the cinema screen.

stories.title: The Youth Film Festival
stories.subtitle: Red Carpets, Awards, and Cheering Viewers
stories.narrative: Every autumn, our town cinema hosts the International Youth Film Festival, welcoming movie lovers from all over Greece. This year, tickets for the opening gala were completely sold out within minutes. Security staff permit ticket holders inside the lobby, but festival rules do not allow visitors to bring outside food. Inside the packed cinema hall, every excited viewer waited with popcorn for the lights to dim. Nobody felt bored, because the varied programme offered something for everyone, representing nearly every cinema genre from comedy to science fiction. After each short film, audience members had a chance to request questions directly to the filmmakers. When the festival jury presented a golden award to a slightly nervous teenager from Thessaloniki, she delivered a moving speech thanking her teachers for believing in her dream.

stories.title: From Page to Big Screen
stories.subtitle: How an Adventure Novel Becomes a Movie
stories.narrative: Turning a popular printed book into a motion picture requires incredible teamwork and creativity. Last year, author Sarah Jenkins watched her thrilling adventure novel become a national bestseller as soon as it hit the shelves across Greece. The original creator wrote about a brave young sailor, and fans fell in love with each memorable character. Soon, a film studio purchased the rights and hired screenwriters to adapt the story into a fast-paced screenplay. In the art studio, an illustrator produced a detailed colour drawing for each key scene, making sure every book illustration came alive. Sarah explained that young writers gain confidence when they develop their ideas with patience. Now, the film version shares the same famous title and promises to thrill cinema crowds around the globe.

stories.title: The Young Critics Circle
stories.subtitle: Debating Plots, Settings, and Villains
stories.narrative: In the media room, the school newspaper film club gathered to write their weekly entertainment column. Student critic Alexis turned on the television just as an announcer reported breaking news about upcoming cinema releases. Alexis praised the exciting plot of the new detective movie, noting how the dark historical setting created brilliant suspense. However, classmate Elena pointed out the makeup: the villain had a crooked nose, a nasty frown, and facial acne to look frightening, while the detective wore a scruffy old coat. The discussion got so lively that someone spilled fruit juice on the floor, and Kostas had to fetch a wet mop to clean the messy table. In their final critique, the club agreed that a strong story and believable acting make a movie unforgettable.

grammar_lab.title: Grammar Lab: Present Simple Passive & Participial Adjectives
grammar_lab.intro: Learn how the Present Simple Passive highlights actions over doers, how -ed and -ing adjectives describe feelings and films, and how to express preferences.

target_structures.name: Present Simple Passive
target_structures.use: Used when the action is more important than who performs it, or when the agent is obvious or unknown.

target_structures.name: -ing vs. -ed Adjectives
target_structures.use: -ing adjectives describe the person, thing, or situation that causes the feeling; -ed adjectives describe how someone feels.

target_structures.name: Expressions of Preference
target_structures.formula: prefer + noun/-ing to + noun/-ing | would rather + bare infinitive than ...
target_structures.use: Expresses likes, choices, and recommendations between leisure options.

rules.explanation: To form the passive in the Present Simple, use the correct form of 'be' (am / is / are) followed by the past participle of the main verb.

examples.sentence: Active: A famous filmmaker directs the new action movie.
examples.highlight: Active focus: the filmmaker performs the action

examples.sentence: Passive: The new action movie is directed by a famous filmmaker.
examples.highlight: Passive focus: the movie receives the action

rules.explanation: Use -ing to describe what the film or book is like. Use -ed to describe how the viewer or reader feels.

examples.sentence: The spy thriller is very exciting.
The viewer is excited when the hero escapes.
The speech was moving, so many people felt moved to tears.

rules.explanation: 'Prefer' takes nouns or gerunds (-ing) joined by 'to'. 'Would rather' takes the bare infinitive joined by 'than'.

examples.sentence: I prefer reading adventure novels to watching comedies.
I would rather see a science fiction film than stay at home.

practice_items.prompt: The new superhero screenplay ______ (write) by a talented young author.
practice_items.explanation: Singular subject 'screenplay' takes 'is written' in the Present Simple Passive.

practice_items.prompt: Hundreds of short movies ______ (show) at the youth film festival every year.
practice_items.explanation: Plural subject 'movies' takes 'are shown' in the passive.

practice_items.prompt: The three-hour documentary was very ______, so the students felt ______ by the end.
practice_items.explanation: The documentary is 'boring' (cause); the students feel 'bored' (emotion).

practice_items.prompt: I prefer watching action films ______ reading long historical novels.
practice_items.explanation: We say 'prefer [doing something] TO [doing something else]'.

practice_items.prompt: Special effects ______ (create) using sophisticated computer software.
practice_items.explanation: Plural subject 'effects' takes 'are created' in the passive.

writing_workshop.title: Writing a Winning Film Review
writing_workshop.prompt: Write a film review for your school magazine about a movie you have recently watched. Include details about the title, director, actors, genre, setting, plot outline, and your recommendation with a star rating.
writing_workshop.model_text:
Title: The Mystery of the Clockwork Spy
Genre: Mystery / Adventure
Director: Paul Greengrass
Starring: Daniel Craig, Emma Watson
Rating: ★★★★★ (5 / 5 stars)

'The Mystery of the Clockwork Spy' is an exciting adventure film directed by Paul Greengrass. The film is set in the rainy streets of London in 1920. Daniel Craig plays Inspector Miller, a clever British detective who receives a secret mission to recover stolen state blueprints.

The plot is fast-paced and full of thrilling surprises. Miller must stop an evil criminal syndicate before midnight. The acting is convincing, and the special effects are sophisticated and believable. What I liked most was the unexpected ending, which kept every viewer guessing until the final minute.

I recommend this film to anyone who enjoys suspenseful detective stories. Don't miss it!

scaffolding.title: Basic Information Header
scaffolding.tip: List the film title, director, main actors, genre, and star rating (e.g. ★★★★☆).

scaffolding.title: Introduction & Setting
scaffolding.tip: Use the Present Simple Passive to state who directed the film and describe the time and place of the setting (e.g. 'The film is directed by... and is set in...').

scaffolding.title: Plot Summary
scaffolding.tip: Briefly describe the main problem and character missions. Never give away the surprise ending!

scaffolding.title: Critique & Recommendation
scaffolding.tip: Use -ing adjectives (exciting, moving, gripping) to explain why viewers should watch it.

self_assessment_checklist: I included a clear header with title, director, and genre.
I used the Present Simple Passive (is directed by, is set in).
I used participial adjectives (-ed and -ing) to express opinions.
I summarized the plot without giving away the ending.
I finished with a clear recommendation and star rating.

can_do_statements.descriptor: I can read and understand texts, articles, and reviews about films, books, and famous characters.
I can use the Present Simple Passive to describe how films are made, directed, and shown.
I can use -ed and -ing adjectives to describe my feelings and the qualities of films and books.
I can express preferences between leisure choices using 'prefer ... to' and 'would rather ... than'.
I can write a structured film review with a plot summary, critical evaluation, and personal recommendation.

teacher_notes.note: Lesson 1 references the super spy genre (James Bond). Emphasize the cultural and literary history of British spy thrillers while ensuring student production focuses on original creative narratives.
Greek learners frequently confuse 'bored' and 'boring'. Use the visual feeling cards in the Grammar Lab to contrast cause ('the movie is boring') with personal feeling ('I am bored').
The Unit 10 project is writing a Film Review. Encourage students to create an illustrated cinema magazine layout for the classroom display wall.
